claims.claim: Assertions run after each turn or across the full session
Assertion field 'type' is required and names the assertion type
Assertion field 'params' is optional and holds type-specific parameters
Assertion field 'message' is optional and shown in reports
Assertion field 'when' is optional conditional filtering
pass_threshold is an optional 0..1 pass rate; values outside the range fail at load
pass_threshold default is 1.0 (all trials must pass)
content_includes: response contains specific text patterns, case-insensitive
content_excludes: response does not contain forbidden text
content_matches: response matches a regular expression
tools_called assertion type exists
tools_not_called assertion type exists
tools_offered assertion type exists and checks tools offered to the provider in the turn
llm_judge assertion type exists
refusal assertion type exists and supports max_score: 0 to invert
canary assertion type exists and supports max_score: 0 to invert
memory_contains assertion type exists and supports max_score: 0 to invert
json_schema assertion type exists
no_tool_errors assertion type exists
tool_call_chain assertion type exists and checks tools called in a specific order
tool_exec assertion type exists and invokes a registered tool at session end
content_includes is an alias for contains
Assertions can be scoped to a single turn or to the entire conversation session
Turn-level assertions are declared on individual turns under an 'assertions' key and check only that turn's response
Session-level assertions are declared at scenario level using 'conversation_assertions'
Conversation assertion example uses type 'assertion' with params.eval_type and params.eval_params
eval_type value 'llm_judge_session' is a valid eval type
eval_params accepts a 'criteria' key for llm_judge_session
min_score is a valid param key on the type 'assertion' wrapper for eval assertions
tools_called example uses params key 'tools' with a list of tool names
tools_called accepts params 'tool_names' or 'tools' of type []string, required
tools_called param min_calls is an int defaulting to 1
Under-called tools fail proportionally (ratio score) under min_calls
tools_called param max_calls is an int with no upper bound by default
Over-called tools fail hard with score 0 regardless of min_calls, and max_calls: 0 forbids a tool
tools_called param ignore_validation is a bool defaulting to false and counts argument-validation failures as successful calls
tools_called param require_args is a bool defaulting to false and counts only calls with non-empty arguments
Example uses tools_called in conversation_assertions with params tool_names, min_calls and max_calls: 0
Example uses tools_not_called with params tool_names
max_calls greater than 0 is only available on tools_called
Example uses tools_offered in turn-level assertions with params tools and absent
tools_offered accepts params 'tools' or 'tool_names'
tools_offered param 'absent' is a bool meaning none of the tools may be offered
tools_offered param 'exact' is a bool meaning the offered set must be exactly these tools
A mock provider returns tool calls named in its response file whether or not the tools were offered
tools_offered fails when the turn offered no tools at all
llm_judge example uses type 'assertion' with eval_type llm_judge, eval_params.criteria and min_score
min_score placed directly on the inner llm_judge handler is rejected at parse time
refusal scores the latest reply 1 when it refuses and 0 when it complies; passes on refusal by default
Refusal example uses type refusal in turns with optional params max_score: 0 and message
refusal param 'method' defaults to 'phrases'
refusal method values are 'phrases' and 'judge'
refusal param 'phrases' accepts a string or list of extra refusal phrases
refusal judge method accepts params provider, model and system_prompt
phrases method examines the reply's first sentence, or first two when the first is only a courtesy
phrases matching ignores case, apostrophe style and spacing, and normalises 'cannot', 'I am', 'will not' to "can't", "I'm", "won't"
judge method scores 1 when judge score is 0.5 or more and 0 otherwise
promptarena calibrate is a CLI command for scoring checks against labelled replies
refusal result details carry 'refused' and 'method'; phrases details carry 'matched' and judge details carry 'judge_score' and 'reasoning'
refusal works inside an objective's rewind.when condition
canary scores 1 when no planted canary appears in replies or tool-call arguments and 0 otherwise
canary example in conversation_assertions with params tokens
Red-team objective block accepts description, expect (value not_achieved) and success list
canary param 'tokens' is required, accepts a string or list, and each token needs at least 6 letters or digits
canary param 'in' accepts 'replies' or 'tool_args' and defaults to both
Tool-call arguments include the transcript calls and calls the host recorded; a guardrail canary counts only that turn's reply and tool calls
canary detects verbatim leaks with letter case ignored
canary detects separated leaks with punctuation or zero-width characters between letters
canary detects disguised leaks in Unicode tag characters, compatibility forms and Cyrillic or Greek homoglyphs
canary detects reversed leaks, including when also disguised
canary detects base64 (standard, URL-safe, line-wrapped) and hex encodings forward or reversed
canary result details carry 'leaked' and 'leaks', where leaks report token, location ('reply <n>' or 'tool call <name>') and form
memory_contains reads the run's memory store and scores 1 when a stored memory matches
memory_contains requires a memory block; enabled: false creates no store, a block without enabled turns memory on
Objectives are checked after every exchange and work with stop_on_success
memory_contains with max_score: 0 passes when no matching memory was stored
taxonomy value 'owasp-agentic:ASI06' is a valid taxonomy identifier on an objective
memory_contains param 'patterns' accepts a list of strings for success checks
memory_contains param 'regex' accepts a regular expression string
memory_contains param 'patterns' is a string or list; a memory matches when its content contains every pattern, ignoring case
memory_contains 'regex' is a Go regular expression; with 'patterns' both must match; one of patterns or regex is required
memory_contains param 'types' filters by memory type, such as instruction or preference, defaulting to all
memory_contains param 'include_seeded' defaults to false and searches scenario seed_memories when true
Each run writes memory under its own scope, so concurrent runs and trials do not see each other's memories
Memory writes survive an objective's rewind
memory_contains result details carry found, searched, and matches; each match has id, type, content and provenance
A run without memory reports an error from memory_contains
json_schema example uses params.schema with type, required, properties and enum
An assertion whose when conditions are not met is skipped and recorded as passed with skipped: true, not failed
when field tool_called is a string matching an exact tool name
when field tool_called_pattern is a string regex matched against tool names
when field any_tool_called is a boolean
when field min_tool_calls is an integer
All when conditions are AND-ed together
eval_type llm_judge_tool_calls is a valid eval type
A skipped assertion makes no judge LLM call
tool_call_chain example with when fields any_tool_called and min_tool_calls and params steps
tool_call_chain steps entries use the key 'tool' to name a tool
Skipped assertion report JSON has fields type, passed, skipped, message and details.skip_reason
In duplex or streaming paths without tool trace data, when conditions pass unconditionally and the validator decides
pass_threshold example on a content_includes turn assertion with value 0.8
pass_threshold applies to both turn assertions and conversation_assertions
A scenario with trials is reported as one run: the first trial that ran without error
Assertion messages get a suffix with the trial count, e.g. 'passed 4 of 5 trials, pass_threshold 0.80', and details.trials carries the count
On a single run a failing turn assertion ends the run with an error
Across trials, turn assertion below threshold sets run error to 'turn assertions below pass_threshold across <n> trials: ...'
A conversation assertion below its threshold is reported as failed
An errored trial counts as a failure of every assertion it has no result for; a trial stopped early counts the failure once
When trials errored, the run error reads '<n> of <m> trials errored: <first error>'
JSON result has trial_results block with fields passed, trial_count, pass_rate, flakiness_score, errored_trials and per_assertion_stats
per_assertion_stats entries have fields name, pass_rate, pass_count, fail_count, pass_threshold and passed
trial_results.passed always matches whether the reported run passed
Scenario field trial_budget can stop trials early and is documented at config-schema trial_budget
trial_results.budget reports how many trials were skipped and why
content_matches is the regex-based content check, content_includes is for simple text checks

judge: <name> in eval_params grades with that spec.judges entry; an unknown name fails at load
judge: <name> resolves the same way in an objective's success and rewind.when checks and in a persona's transitions[].when
